after.author_corresponding_institution: Berry Consultants, LLC, Austin, Texas 78746, United States
after.abstract: The Path to Prevention (P2P) platform trial is a first-in-class, phase 2A, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled learning study. Its design expedites the assessment of investigational therapies for the treatment of early-stage Neuronal a-Synuclein Disease (NSD), a biological disease continuum that encompasses and often precedes clinically manifest Parkinson's Disease. P2P is embedded within the Parkinson's Precision Medicine Initiative (PPMI), a robust observational longitudinal cohort study on Parkinson's disease progression and a trial-facilitating enrollment framework. A regimen, comprised of an active investigational therapy and a matched placebo control, evaluates a therapeutic candidate within the P2P perpetual platform framework. Multiple regimens can be enrolled, enabling efficient testing of multiple therapeutics. A two-stage randomization scheme determines regimen sample size with 125 participants assigned to a regimen's active therapy and a variable number to placebo control. The treated follow up period is a minimum of 96 weeks and a maximum of 144 weeks, with the last randomized participant followed for 96 weeks. As a pioneering interventional trial in early-stage NSD, P2P endpoint selection was critically informed by modeling and analysis of available PPMI data. In P2P, regimens will be evaluated for efficacy using two primary endpoints: 1) a biomarker outcome of Dopamine Transporter Single-Photon Emission Computed Tomography (DAT SPECT) imaging measured by the bilateral putamen Specific Binding Ratio (SBR) and 2) a clinical outcome measured by the Movement Disorder Society-Sponsored Revision of the Unified Parkinson's Disease Rating Scale (MDS-UPDRS) Part III score. Each endpoint will be assessed separately using a longitudinal Bayesian mixed effects model, which compares the active treatment group to the shared placebo control group. The model uses regimen-specific controls at full weight and dynamically discounts controls from other regimens. Additionally, placebo control estimates are supplemented by non-randomized control data from the PPMI cohort. Clinical trial simulations, informed by longitudinal data from 275 P2P-eligible PPMI study participants (Age 60-81, 35% Female, 65% Male), were conducted to evaluate the design. Each regimen is well-powered to detect a 40% slowing in progression for both the clinical and biomarker primary endpoints when comparing active treatment to randomized control data. Supplementing the control estimation with non-randomized, P2P-eligible registry participant data increases power in the explored scenarios up to 4% for each endpoint. The embedded P2P platform trial is a powerful learning study that leverages statistical efficiencies from the platform trial design and established PPMI infrastructure and is poised to advance treatment development in early-stage NSD.

after.abstract: The development of biologically targeted therapeutics (BTTs) that slow Parkinson's disease progression has been hampered by a reliance on testing interventions in clinically defined populations with already advanced pathobiology. Publications on the biological definition and classification of neuronal a-synuclein disease (NSD), and the development of the NSD integrated staging system (NSD-ISS), have generated a framework for identifying individuals with NSD prior to the emergence of a clinically defined syndrome. Path to Prevention (P2P) is a phase 2A, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled platform trial designed to assess the safety and efficacy of interventions in an early-stage NSD population. The trial is embedded within the observational Parkinson's Precision Medicine Initiative (PPMI), a structure that enables recruitment of participants from the PPMI cohort, leverages existing operational infrastructure, and utilizes data from non-P2P enrolled PPMI participants in the Bayesian statistical modeling. P2P will enroll participants at least 60 years of age with NSD Stage 2B (abnormal -synuclein, dopaminergic dysfunction, and prodromal signs or symptoms without functional impairment) without a clinically defined diagnosis of PD or a related disorder. As a platform trial, P2P will enable the testing of multiple interventions under a Master Protocol at approximately 35 sites across North America and Europe. Interventions are selected from industry-submitted applications based on biological relevance of the targets, and on the adequacy of the safety data appropriate to the target population. Each treatment regimen will have 125 participants on active treatment and at least 125 shared placebo control participants. Participants will remain on treatment for a maximum of 144 weeks or until 96 weeks since the randomization of the last participant. P2P has two primary endpoints, 1) rate of change in mean putamen specific binding ratio from baseline through follow-up and, 2) rate of change in the MDS-UPDRS Part III motor examination from baseline through follow-up or initiation of dopaminergic treatment. A range of secondary and exploratory biomarker-focused endpoints will be assessed. The protocol was developed with input from multiple stakeholders, including people with early-stage NSD, biopharmaceutical industry leaders, and regulatory authorities. P2P is the first trial to test biologically targeted assets in biologically defined prodromal participants utilizing an efficient platform design, which will provide the field with tools to expand therapeutic development, and enable intervention at earlier stages of neurodegeneration. P2P is scheduled to begin enrollment in December 2026 and is committed to data sharing and broad dissemination of learnings from the study.

after.authors: Habibzadeh, P.; Zhao, K.; Cenname, A.; Jan, Y. J. A.; Geramita, E. M.; Im, A. P.; Sorkin, J. D.; Bick, A. G.; Hsu, D. J.
after.author_corresponding_institution: The Ohio State University Comprehensive Cancer Center
after.abstract: Clonal hematopoiesis of indeterminate potential (CHIP) is a recognized precursor of myeloid malignancy and an independent cardiovascular risk factor, but its relationship with solid tumors is incompletely defined, particularly at histologic resolution. Here, we quantify the association between CHIP and incident cancer across hematologic and solid-organ sites, by clone size, mutation number, and histologic subtype in a prospective cohort of UK Biobank participants with baseline genetic sequencing and cancer ascertained by national registry linkage; those with pre-baseline cancer were excluded. Vanderbilt BioVU was used for replication. CHIP was associated with any incident cancer (HR, 1.22; 95% CI, 1.18-1.27) and with all solid tumors combined (HR, 1.13; 95% CI, 1.08-1.19). Among 17 endpoints, two survived multiple testing correction: lung adenocarcinoma (HR, 1.79; 95% CI, 1.48 - 2.16) and esophageal squamous cell carcinoma (HR, 2.28; 95% CI, 1.37-3.81). Risk increased with clone size and multi-hit CHIP, most markedly for esophageal cancer (VAF [≥]30%: HR, 2.72), and the esophageal squamous association persisted in 5-year landmark analysis (HR, 2.57). In BioVU, CHIP was directionally associated with esophageal cancer and lung adenocarcinoma and its association with all solid tumors overall (HR, 1.24; 95% CI, 1.17-1.32) was confirmed. These findings extend CHIP from a hematologic and cardiovascular risk marker to a risk marker of solid-organ cancer risk with histologic resolution and motivate clone-size aware risk models and mechanistic studies.

after.authors: Pohlman, A.; Marten, A. D.; Fontes Noronha, M.; Khemmani, M.; Wolfe, A.; Abdelsattar, Z. M.
after.author_corresponding_institution: Loyola University Chicago Stritch School of Medicine
after.abstract: Background: The lung fosters a diverse microbiome that may have a complex interplay with underlying diseases, such as lung cancer. However, existing literature has revealed diverse results, likely owing to small sample sizes and diverse sampling methods. In this context, we aim to characterize the lung microbiome and its association with malignancy via multiple sampling methods during lung resection. Methods: Patients undergoing lung resection for confirmed malignancy were prospectively included in the study. During the operation, a bronchial swab and a parenchymal biopsy of lung tissue were collected from the resected specimen and sent for analysis via 16S rRNA gene amplicon (V4) sequencing. An established bioinformatics pipeline was used to determine taxonomic identification and compare these results to clinical and tumor data. Results: There were 83 participants included, with 75 (90.4%) patients having primary lung tumors and 8 (9.6%) having metastatic lesions. Resections included lobectomy (69.9%), wedge (25.3%), and segmentectomy (4.8%). Lung microbiome composition differed by primary malignancy site (lung vs metastatic; p=0.014) and tumor mutations (TP53, p=0.040; KRAS, p=0.054). For primary lung cancer, there was no difference in microbiome composition by tumor histology. A near-significant association was noted for patients with prolonged air leaks and alpha diversity of the lung microbiome (p=0.070). Conclusions: In this study, we demonstrate associations between the lung microbiome and underlying malignancy and tumor characteristics. Validation of these results may assist with diagnostic, prognostic, and therapeutic interventions in the operative and peri-operative management of lung cancer.

after.authors: Tsaggaris, J. C.; Mimouni, N.; Judy, R. L.; Xue, D.; Morley, M. P.; Wang, X.; Cotney, J. L.; Kelly, D. P.; Day, S. M.; Cappola, T. P.; Penn Medicine BioBank,  ; Damrauer, S. M.; Levin, M. G.
after.author_corresponding_institution: Division of Cardiovascular Medicine, Department of Medicine; Department of Genetics; Cardiovascular Institute, Perelman School of Medicine, University of Pennsy
after.abstract: Cardiac remodeling underlies cardiomyopathy and heart failure, yet how common genetic effects are organized across the four chambers, and whether they influence phenotypic variability beyond additive genetic effects, remains unclear. We analyzed 22 cardiac magnetic resonance phenotypes in up to 77,271 UK Biobank participants. Additive mapping identified 748 locus-trait associations across 239 regions. Multivariate fine-mapping revealed that 96% of signals showed effects across multiple cardiac chambers, while resolving independent signals with distinct anatomical profiles, including predominantly atrial and ventricular signals at RBM20. Fine-mapped signal sharing formed three robust communities corresponding broadly to atrial function, chamber remodeling and ventricular systolic function. Variance mapping identified 19 associations, 13 without a nearby additive signal. Individual variance loci and polygenic effects generalized to clinical echocardiographic phenotypes and outcomes in the Penn Medicine Biobank. These findings reveal cardiac common-variant architecture as broadly shared yet locally heterogeneous and identify phenotypic variability as a partly distinct genetic dimension.

after.title: Preprint: An explainable, bias-audited machine learning model to detect hidden hepatitis C from region-wide real-world health records
after.authors: Esteban-Medina, A.; Loucera, C.; Dopazo, J.; Romero Gomez, M.
after.abstract: Background: Although direct-acting antivirals have transformed hepatitis C virus (HCV) treatment, 25-30% of active infections in Spain remain undiagnosed. We aimed to develop and validate an interpretable machine-learning model to identify undiagnosed HCV infection using only data already recorded within the health system. Materials and Methods: We conducted a retrospective, population-based cohort study using the Andalusian Population Health Database (BPS). Individuals diagnosed with HCV between 2017 and 2024 (n=25,028) were matched, up to 10:1, to controls by birth year, sex, and health district. An Explainable Boosting Machine was trained on 2017-2022 data, with a threshold set in a 2023 validation set to guarantee [≥]60% sensitivity, then evaluated unmodified in an independent, non-matched, population-representative 2024 sample approximating real-world screening. Predictors comprised chronic-disease diagnoses and laboratory summary statistics recorded [≥]30 days before the index date; age and sex were excluded as matching variables. Predictors reflecting socioeconomic proxies or matching artefacts (pharmaceutical co-payment category, a zone-level deprivation index) were removed after explainability review. Results: In the independent test set, the model achieved an AUC of 0.837 (0.826 in validation), sensitivity 63.5%, specificity 91.8%, positive predictive value 7.0%, and negative predictive value 99.6%. Leading predictors were minimum alanine aminotransferase, HIV infection, dependence on non-tobacco substances, and platelet-count statistics, forming a clinically coherent, laboratory- and comorbidity-driven profile. Conclusion: An explainable model built exclusively from routine electronic health record data can identify undiagnosed HCV infection with discrimination comparable to previously published tools, evaluated under conditions approximating true population prevalence. Bias-auditing was feasible without sacrificing interpretability, supporting a scalable, equity-conscious instrument for the final phase of HCV elimination.

after.title: Preprint: A Cross-Dataset Audit of Discrimination and Conformal Prediction Coverage in Keystroke-Based Parkinson's Disease Classi cation
after.authors: Guang, H.; Zhang, Z.; Qu, J.; Ma, J.; Wu, J.
after.abstract: Typing dynamics are being investigated as a digital behavioral marker for Parkinson's disease (PD), but the cross-dataset reliability of typing-based classi ers remains uncertain. We evaluated four public datasets (475 par ticipants; 270 with PD and 205 controls) across 12 transfer directions using split conformal prediction targeting 90% marginal coverage. In all three pri mary directions, coverage was below the 0.90 target and the one-sided tests remained signi cant after Holm correction: 0.598 (95% CI, 0.4830.704) for Tappy[->]MIT, 0.850 (0.7880.899) for MIT[->]Tappy, and 0.732 (0.6840.777) for clinical[->]self-reported transfer. Discrimination and coverage did not con sistently change together: LightGBM had lower AUC than logistic regression in all 12 directions but higher coverage in 11, with larger prediction sets. Class-conditional coverage varied by target cohort: PD-conditional cover age was 0.214 for Tappy[->]MIT, whereas healthy-control coverage was 0.700 for MIT[->]Tappy and 0.627 for clinical[->]self-reported transfer. Recalibration with 9 and 18 labeled target participants raised the lower condence bound above 0.80 in the latter two directions; in Tappy[->]MIT, it remained below 0.80 even with 25 labels. Weighted conformal prediction yielded coverage of 0.9181.000 without target labels but returned the full label set for 86% 100% of participants. Stress tests did not reproduce the observed coverage patterns, and black-box shift estimation did not support pure label shift as the dominant explanation for Tappy[->]MIT. Evaluating typing dynamics as a digital marker for PD requires cross-dataset assessment of discrimination, marginal and class-conditional coverage, and recovery costs. Clinical screen ing utility has not been established.

after.authors: Lane, A.; Hay, K.; Sivakumaran, S.; Dolby, H.; Winlaw, S.; Wise, D.; Muruganandah, V.; Heraganahally, S.; Lalwani, N.-I.; Eustace, M.; Chui, F.; Kelly, T.; Redmond, A.; Chapman, P. R.; Chaudhuri, A.; Vemuri, K.; Burke, A.; McNamara, J.; Barber, B. E.; Horvath, R.
after.abstract: Objectives Persistent methicillin-susceptible Staphylococcus aureus (MSSA) bacteraemia is associated with significant morbidity and mortality. Cefazolin-ertapenem combination therapy has demonstrated synergistic activity in preclinical models and small case series, but comparative clinical evidence is lacking. Methods We conducted a multicentre retrospective review of all patients aged >18 years with persistent MSSA bacteraemia at two Queensland tertiary hospitals between January 2014 and December 2024. The primary outcome was time to blood culture sterilisation, compared between patients who commenced cefazolin-ertapenem combination therapy prior to first negative blood culture and a matched cohort of non-combination-treated patients. Secondary outcomes included 90-day all-cause mortality, 90-day relapse, development of multi-resistant organisms, Clostridioides difficile infection, and adverse drug events. Results A total of 288 episodes of persistent MSSA bacteraemia in 283 patients were identified. Twenty-six patients received cefazolin-ertapenem combination therapy. Among the 14 patients who commenced combination therapy prior to first negative blood culture, median time to sterilisation was 1 day (IQR 1 - 2), compared with 2 days (IQR 1 - 3) in the matched non-combination group. Cox regression in the matched cohort (n=114) demonstrated an increased rate of blood culture clearance with combination therapy (HR 1.8; 95% CI 1.2 - 2.7; P =0.004). In the full cohort, ninety-day mortality (20.0% vs 23.0%, P=0.73) and relapse rates (11.5% vs 8.3%, P =0.57) did not differ significantly between groups. Conclusions Cefazolin-ertapenem combination therapy was associated with accelerated blood culture sterilisation in persistent MSSA bacteraemia. Prospective randomised evaluation is warranted.

after.title: Preprint: A CBC-derived score associated with dengue NS1 antigen positivity among suspected dengue patients in Dhaka: a retrospective model-development study
after.authors: Nishan, R. K.; Alam, M. S.; Azad, A. K.; Sarkar, M. M. H.; Nodee, T. A.; Mia, M. Z.; Miah, M. I.; Islam, M. S.
after.author_corresponding_institution: Department of Microbiology, Jagannath University, Dhaka, Bangladesh
after.abstract: Background: Early diagnostic triage for suspected dengue is important in high-volume settings, yet confirmatory testing may be delayed or intermittently available. This study aimed to develop and internally validate a simple complete blood count (CBC)-derived score to estimate the likelihood of same-day dengue non-structural protein 1 (NS1) antigen positivity among suspected dengue patients in Dhaka, Bangladesh. Methods: We conducted a retrospective model-development study at Uttara Adhunik Medical College Hospital using data from patients with clinical suspicion of dengue between 19 August and 12 October 2023. The final analysis included 596 unique patients who underwent CBC and NS1 testing on the same day. Least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO) penalized logistic regression was used for variable selection among routinely available demographic and hematological predictors. Selected predictors were refit using unpenalized logistic regression to derive a CBC score. Internal validation and calibration were assessed using bootstrap optimism correction with 400 resamples. Results: Among 596 patients, 306 (51.3%) were NS1 positive. The final parsimonious model retained platelet count rescaled per 10 x 109/L, white blood cell count, and monocyte count. The optimism-corrected AUC was 0.9429. At the Youden-derived cutoff of 11.825, the final integer score had sensitivity 0.833 (95% CI, 0.787-0.873), specificity 0.966 (95% CI, 0.938-0.983), PPV 0.962 (95% CI, 0.932-0.982), NPV 0.846 (95% CI, 0.802-0.883), and accuracy 0.898 (95% CI, 0.870-0.921). A rounded cutoff of 12 produced similar performance. In benchmark analysis, the final model showed a modest improvement over platelet count alone (AUC 0.944 vs 0.931; Delta AUC 0.012; DeLong p=0.00364). Conclusion: A three-parameter CBC score can estimate the likelihood of NS1 antigen positivity among suspected dengue patients in this single-center dataset. The score should be interpreted as a CBC-only triage adjunct, not as a replacement for confirmatory dengue testing. External validation in independent cohorts is needed before routine clinical use.

after.title: Preprint: Hypoxic Burden Predicts Symptomatic but Not Sleep Architecture Response to CPAP Therapy in Obstructive Sleep Apnea
after.authors: Baecker, S.; Ehrlich, F.; Sehr, T.; Brandt, M.; Sedlmayr, M.; Goldammer, M.
after.author_corresponding_institution: TU Dresden Faculty of Medicine Carl Gustav Carus: Technische Universitat Dresden Medizinische Fakultat Carl Gustav Carus
after.abstract: The apnea-hypopnea index (AHI) remains the standard metric for assessing obstructive sleep apnea (OSA) severity, although it does not fully capture the physiological consequences of respiratory events. Hypoxic burden (HB), which integrates the frequency, depth, and duration of oxygen desaturations, has been proposed as a more comprehensive measure of OSA-related hypoxic stress. This study compared the prognostic value of HB and AHI for subjective and objective treatment outcomes in patients undergoing continuous positive airway pressure (CPAP) therapy. Data from 412 patients with OSA who underwent diagnostic and CPAP-treated polysomnography were analyzed, including 52 patients with available follow-up questionnaires. HB was calculated using a validated event-based algorithm. Multivariable regression models were used to predict patient-reported outcomes and changes in sleep architecture, adjusted for age, sex and body mass index. HB consistently demonstrated stronger associations with symptomatic outcomes than AHI. Models including HB showed improved model fit and explained variance. HB remained independently associated with lower follow-up fatigue and better sleep quality after adjustment for AHI. In contrast, AHI was the dominant predictor of objective sleep architecture improvements, including increases in N3 sleep, reductions in N1 sleep, and reductions in arousal index. HB provided additional independent information only for changes in arousal burden. These findings suggest that HB and AHI capture complementary dimensions of OSA severity. While AHI primarily reflects sleep fragmentation and physiological response to CPAP, HB appears more closely related to subjective treatment benefit. Incorporating HB alongside AHI may improve clinical phenotyping and prediction of treatment response in OSA.

after.title: Preprint: Biomarker-Informed Phenotyping of the Heart Failure Continuum: A Population-Based Evaluation of the Second Universal Definition of Heart Failure
after.authors: Chen, H.; Ye, J.
after.abstract: Objective: To develop and evaluate a biomarker-informed, computable phenotype of the heart failure (HF) continuum, aligned with 2026 AHA/ACC/ESC/WHF Expert Consensus, using NHANES and linked mortality data, and to determine whether this phenotype identifies subgroups with distinct mortality risks. Methods: We analyzed 11,477 U.S. adults aged [≥]20 years from the 1999-2004 NHANES cycles who participated in the surplus-sera biomarker substudy and were linked to National Death Index follow-up. Participants were classified into four phenotypes according to the 2026 Universal Definition of Heart Failure: no apparent risk, Stage A (at risk), Stage B (elevated NT-proBNP without self-reported HF), and Stage C (self-reported HF). Survey-weighted Kaplan-Meier curves and nested, multiply imputed Cox proportional hazards models, with sequential adjustment for demographic, socioeconomic, and cardiometabolic covariates, were used to estimate associations with mortality. Pairwise phenotype comparisons, standardized adjusted survival estimates, and restricted mean survival times were also calculated. Incremental prognostic value was evaluated by comparing discrimination and reclassification metrics between the full phenotype and a conventional three-level model that excluded NT-proBNP. Results: Weighted prevalences were 16.9%, 70.0%, 10.7%, and 2.4% for no apparent risk, Stage A, Stage B, and Stage C, respectively. In fully adjusted models, the hazard ratios (HRs) relative to no apparent risk were 1.58 (95% CI, 1.08-2.30), 2.88 (95% CI, 2.00-4.16), and 2.56 (95% CI, 1.61-4.09), respectively. Stage B was associated with significantly higher mortality risk than Stage A (HR, 1.83; 95% CI, 1.62-2.07), whereas the difference between Stage C and Stage B was not statistically significant (HR, 0.89; 95% CI, 0.71-1.11). The association for Stage B attenuated less across sequentially adjusted models than that for Stage C. Adjusted 10-year mortality risks were 15.2% for Stage B and 14.2% for Stage C. Incorporating Stage B into the conventional model yielded only marginal improvements in discrimination ({Delta}C-statistic, 0.002; 95% CI, 0.001-0.002). Conclusion: A biomarker-informed phenotype of the HF continuum can be operationalized using national survey data and identifies a pre-HF subgroup with an adjusted mortality risk not significantly different from that of individuals with overt HF, despite only marginal gains in prognostic discrimination.

items.title: Preprint: Lesion sterilisation and tissue repair with chloramphenicol, tetracycline, zinc oxide-eugenol paste compared to zinc oxide-eugenol pulpectomy in primary molars: Two-year follow-up findings of a multicentre non-inferiority randomised clinical trial

after.abstract: Background: Chloramphenicol, tetracycline, zinc oxide (CTZ) paste has been widely used, particularly in Latin America, in Lesion Sterilization and Tissue Repair (LSTR) procedures in primary molars. However, reports on its long-term efficacy are scarce. Aim: This multicentre non-inferiority randomised trial compared the efficacy of LSTR using CTZ paste with conventional zinc oxide-eugenol (ZOE) pulpectomy in primary molars. Design: 199 primary molars from children aged 3 to 9 years were randomised to the CTZ or ZOE groups. The primary outcome was clinical and radiographic success at 24 months. Clinical time, children's behaviour, immediate discomfort and postoperative pain were also evaluated. The main analysis followed the intention-to-treat (ITT) principle, comparing success proportions with the Miettinen-Nurminen method, considering a prespecified non-inferiority margin of 15% (p < 0.05). Results: Overall success rates in the ITT population were 64.3% for CTZ and 58.7% for ZOE, with a difference of 5.6% (95% CI: -9.3 to 20.4; p<0.01). Mean; standard deviation clinical time was significantly shorter in CTZ (36.3; 9.8 min) than in ZOE (63.0; 16.3 min) (p<0.01). Children's behaviour, immediate discomfort and postoperative pain were similar between groups (p>0.05). Conclusion: LSTR with CTZ paste was non-inferior to conventional ZOE pulpectomy after 24 months of follow-up.

after.title: Preprint: Positive islet autoantibodies confirm classical type 1 diabetes in patients treated as type 2 diabetes who have early progression to insulin
after.authors: Simpson, V. E.; Thomas, N. J. M.; Hill, A. V.; Knupp, J.; McDonald, T. J.; Patel, K. A.; Murray Leech, J. A.; Shields, B. M.; Pearson, E. R.; Jones, A. G.
after.abstract: Objective: Early progression to insulin following initial management as type 2 diabetes may indicate missed type 1 diabetes. Recent guidelines advise islet-autoantibody testing in all adults who progress to insulin within 3 years, though this has not been directly tested. We aimed to determine whether positive islet autoantibodies in this setting confirm the genetic characteristics and C-peptide progression of classical type 1 diabetes. Research Design and Methods: We compared genetic susceptibility to type 1 and type 2 diabetes (T1DGRS and T2DGRS) and prospectively assessed C-peptide loss over 3 years after diagnosis among islet-autoantibody-positive adults initially treated as having type 2 diabetes (without insulin) who progressed to insulin within 3 years (n=86), versus participants with classical type 1 (n=499) and type 2 (n=603) diabetes. Results were replicated in cross-sectional data from the DARE/GoDARTS studies (n=9466). Results: Participants who progressed to insulin within 3 years and had positive islet autoantibodies had the genetic characteristics and C-peptide loss of classical type 1 diabetes: T1DGRS -0.04 (-0.27, 0.18) vs 0.00 (-0.09, 0.09) [p=0.71], T2DGRS -0.35 (-0.59, -0.11) vs -0.35 (-0.44, -0.26) [p=0.99] and annual change in urine C-peptide creatinine ratio -47% (-55%, -40%) vs -49% (-52%, -46%) [p=0.6] respectively. In contrast, autoantibody-positive participants without early insulin (n=51) had genetic and C-peptide characteristics consistent with type 2 diabetes. Findings were similar in cross-sectional cohorts. Conclusion: Islet-autoantibody-positive individuals with early insulin requirement following initial treatment as type 2 diabetes have similar genotype and progression to classical type 1 diabetes. This supports recent guidance that they should be diagnosed and treated as type 1 diabetes.

after.authors: Brittain, J.-S.; Mills, C.; Judge, C.; Bastos, L. S.; Freitas, L. P.; Carvalho, L. M.; Araujo, E. C.; Coelho, F. C.; Xu, Y.; Reddy, B.; Pasumarthi, R. K.; Shekel, T.; Shetty, S.; Chou, A. C.-Y.; Carter, A.; Muslim, A.; Prasad, G.; Widner, K.; Bharel, M.; Scarpino, S. V.; Flaxman, S.; Bhatt, S.; Tsui, J. L. H.; Kraemer, M. U. G.
after.abstract: Accurate and timely probabilistic dengue forecasts can support public health preparedness, but producing reliable forecasts across locations and time horizons remains challenging. We evaluated five statistical, machine-learning, deep-learning, and foundation-model approaches for forecasting monthly reported dengue cases across 5,570 Brazilian municipalities at 1-, 3-, 6- and 12-month horizons, with forecasts backtested from January 2020 to August 2025. The time-series foundation model TimesFM maintained comparatively stable probabilistic forecast performance at longer horizons, while most other models showed declining performance. We then tested whether spatial representations of human and environmental context from a Population Dynamics Foundation Model (PDFM) could improve forecasts through post-hoc residual adjustment. PDFM adjustment improved mean probabilistic forecast performance, measured by the Weighted Interval Score (WIS), in 19 of 20 model-horizon combinations, although the magnitude and frequency of improvements varied across models, horizons and municipalities. The largest improvements were observed for N-BEATS, including a reduction in mean WIS of 1.13 at the six-month horizon (95% CI [0.84, 1.48]; Diebold-Mariano p < 0.0001), with improvements also observed for XGBoost. The proportion of forecasts improved by PDFM generally increased with locally reported dengue case counts, although this relationship varied between models. Covariate selection, spatial fitting and forecast aggregation strategies showed strong model-dependent effects, while monthly model retraining provided no consistent advantage in the settings evaluated. Together, these findings highlight the potential of pretrained representations for dengue forecasting, with benefits dependent on forecasting architecture, horizon and modelling configuration.

after.title: Preprint: Time to sustained control of the effective reproduction number as a failure-time estimand: a county-level analysis of the first SARS-CoV-2 wave in the United States.
after.authors: Kakasis, A.; Panagiotidou, M.; Demiris, N.; Samoli, E.; Sypsa, V.
after.author_corresponding_institution: Department of Preventive Medicine, Epidemiology and Medical Statistics, School of Medicine, National and Kapodistrian University of Athens, Greece.
after.abstract: Subnational analyses of emerging pathogen transmission typically model the reproduction number (Rt) as a continuous outcome and estimate average associations with its level. Operationally, however, response planning depends on a different quantity: which jurisdictions bring transmission below the epidemic threshold (Rt<1), and how quickly. We formulate time to control as a failure-time estimand and show that doing so exposes a structural feature that linear regression does not accommodate: a jurisdiction cannot enter the risk set until enough cases accumulate to estimate Rt. Cases accumulate faster where transmission is faster, so entry time depends on the outcome process itself and on factors that drive early spread. We account for this outcome-dependent observability using a mixed-effects Cox proportional hazards model with calendar-time left truncation and state-level Gaussian frailties, applied to 2,956 US counties observed between January 22 and July 15, 2020. The primary event was defined as the first three-day sustained reduction of mean Rt below one. Control was rare (171 counties, 5.8%). Each standard-deviation increase in log population density was associated with a lower rate of control (hazard ratio 0.54; 95% confidence interval 0.44 - 0.67) and higher policy stringency with a faster rate (HR 1.50; CI 1.09 - 2.05). Evaluating jurisdictions by their rate of reaching an operational target - rather than by average transmission level - provides a clearer, decision-relevant metric for prospective allocation decisions and public health interventions. Keywords: SARS-CoV-2, COVID-19, reproduction number, survival analysis, Cox model, county-level, United States, policy stringency, population density.

after.title: Preprint: Greater than the sum of its parts: A novel psychiatric multimorbidity metric applied to rare disease
after.authors: Pollak, R. M.; Sefik, E.; Klaiman, C.; Bishop, D. V.; Harner, M. K.; Khan, A.; Purcell, J. R.; Wheeler, M.; Irving, T.; Pulver, S.; Cubells, J. F.; Walker, E. F.; Murphy, M. M.; Mulle, J. G.
after.abstract: Importance: Rare genetic syndromes are often drivers of complex multimorbidity. However, current methods consider multimorbidity as the sum of chronic diagnoses, which does not account for subthreshold impairment. Objective: To develop a quantitative multimorbidity score (MMS) for rare genetic syndromes that summarizes the neurodevelopmental and psychiatric multimorbidity landscape, including subthreshold symptoms, using 3q29 deletion and 3q29 duplication syndromes as hallmark examples. Design: We developed a multimorbidity metric and applied it to cross-sectional data. Remote phenotyping from 2023-2026. In-person phenotyping from 2017-2020. Setting: Remote phenotyping conducted at Rutgers University. In-person phenotyping conducted at Emory University. Participants: Participants were 6 years of age and older. 3q29del and 3q29dup recruited from the 3q29 registry and direct referrals and contacts. Syndrome status confirmed by genetic report review. Typically developing controls recruited from community sources and ResearchMatch. Main Outcomes and Measures: We developed a quantitative MMS across five distinct domains of functioning, operationalized as the sum of z-scores across six standardized assessments. The MMS was calculated for each study participant and compared across groups. Within 3q29del, we evaluated the relationship between MMSs and Vineland-3 adaptive behavior. Results: 96 individuals with 3q29del (52.08% male, 18.01+/-11.47 years old), 28 individuals with 3q29dup (50.00% male, 20.82+/-13.64 years old), and 53 controls (41.51% male, 17.77+/-10.74 years old) were included. 3q29del and 3q29dup participants had significantly lower MMS scores compared to controls (3q29del mean=-8.22+/-4.67, 3q29dup mean=-6.47+/-4.66, control mean=1.36+/-2.35, 3q29del p<2E-16, 3q29dup p=4.89E-16). Within 3q29del, subjects with more severe multimorbidity had greater impairment in adaptive behavior (R2=0.589, p<2E-16). The quantitative MMS is more highly correlated with adaptive behavior than traditional diagnosis-based multimorbidity metrics (quantitative MMS R2=0.589, diagnosis-based multimorbidity R2=0.447). In a subset of 24 3q29del participants with longitudinal data (58.33% male, 13.17+/-9.08 years old at first evaluation, average time to follow up=5.17+/-0.87 years), the MMS is stable over time (R2=0.858, p=8.34E-8). Conclusions and Relevance: Our novel quantitative MMS is an improved metric for measuring psychiatric multimorbidity in high-risk populations, and accounts for the impact of subthreshold impairments. When applied to 3q29del and 3q29dup, it quantifies the individual burden of multimorbidity, is stable over time, and is associated with clinical outcome measures.

after.abstract: Background: Kangaroo Mother Care (KMC) reduces neonatal mortality and morbidity among preterm and low birthweight (LBW) infants, but implementation and quality vary across sub-Saharan African (SSA) hospitals. This study reports KMC coverage and quality of care for preterm and LBW neonates admitted to hospitals in the NEST360 Alliance (Kenya, Malawi, Tanzania, Nigeria) and examines the association between KMC provision and survival to discharge. Methods: We conducted a cross-sectional study using routinely collected neonatal inpatient data from hospitals participating in the NEST360 Alliance. Newborns weighing under 2500g were eligible for KMC and included in coverage and quality analyses (January 2021-December 2024). Quality-of-care cascades quantified attrition along the KMC care pathway from eligibility to successful delivery, defining quality as the proportion of eligible neonates reaching each successive step. Mixed-effects logistic regression assessed the association between KMC and survival at discharge, including variation by illness severity and, among KMC recipients, by timing of initiation across severity and birthweight strata. Results: Of 375,238 neonatal admissions across 66 hospitals, 125,844 neonates were eligible for KMC and had KMC documentation available. Among these, 64,619 (51.3%) received KMC. All four countries showed improved coverage over the study period, with the largest absolute increases in Nigeria (27.6%) and Tanzania (27.4%). Excluding Kenya, where KMC timing data were unavailable, 92.1% of neonates started on KMC had a documented start date; of these 44,264 neonates, 12,934 (29.2%) were initiated on KMC on the first day of life. The quality cascade showed eligible neonates were lost at each step, from eligibility through to documented, timely, and sustained KMC. Among neonates eligible for both KMC and CPAP, 39.4% of those started on KMC also received documented CPAP at some point during admission. After adjustment for patient-level factors, receiving KMC was associated with improved survival across all severity groups, with the greatest absolute benefit among the most critically ill neonates (adjusted predicted survival 7% vs 80% without and with KMC, respectively). Conclusion: KMC coverage improved substantially across NEST360-implementing hospitals between 2021 and 2024, demonstrating progress in implementation. However, important gaps remain in the quality and timeliness of KMC delivery. More investment in high-quality KMC implementation, supported by robust monitoring systems linked with quality improvement, are essential to improve outcomes for small and sick newborns across sub-Saharan Africa.

after.abstract: Background: Lung function is a key indicator of respiratory health and is known to be influenced by lifestyle practices such as yoga. Recent advances in artificial intelligence (AI) have enabled non-invasive, scalable, and real-time assessment of physiological parameters. Swaasa is an AI-based novel technique designed to assess lung function through cough analysis, offering a potential alternative to conventional spirometry. Objective: The present study aimed to evaluate lung function using Swaasa among yoga practitioners and compare the findings with age- and sex-matched non-yoga practitioners in a cross-sectional design. Methods: A cross-sectional comparative study was conducted on adult participants divided into two groups: regular yoga practitioners ([≥]1 year of practice) and non-yoga practitioners. Lung function parameters, including Forced Vital Capacity (FVC), Forced Expiratory Volume in one second (FEV), and cough pattern indices, were assessed using the Swaasa AI-based system. Results: Yoga practitioners demonstrated significantly higher AI-derived lung function indices, including FVC and FEV, compared to non-yoga practitioners (p < 0.05). Improved respiratory health and reduced respiratory variability were also observed in the yoga group, indicating enhanced respiratory efficiency. Conclusion: The findings suggest that regular yoga practice is associated with better lung function as assessed by Swaasa.

after.abstract: Background: Systemic sclerosis (SSc) and dermatomyositis (DM) are autoimmune diseases that have been proposed as models of cancer immunoediting. Autoantibody-defined subsets show divergent cancer risks, yet malignancy often remains clinically occult. We tested whether circulating tumor DNA (ctDNA) can reveal subclinical cancer in new-onset SSc and DM. Methods: We prospectively recruited adults with recent SSc or DM onset. Plasma ctDNA was assessed using a targeted next-generation sequencing panel covering commonly mutated cancer genes. Patients were followed for 18-24 months on average. ctDNA positivity was correlated with subsequent cancer diagnoses. Findings: Among 134 patients (69 SSc, 65 DM), cancer was diagnosed in six (4.5%; three SSc, three DM). ctDNA was detected in four of these six patients (67%) a median of 13 months (range 1.4-17) before clinical diagnosis; in three of four patients, mutations detected in plasma matched those subsequently identified in the same patients primary tumors. ctDNA was also detected in 16 of 128 patients without a cancer diagnosis. ctDNA positivity conferred an 11.4-fold higher risk of malignancy relative to ctDNA negativity and yielded a negative predictive value of 98% and a positive predictive value of 20% for cancer within the observation window. Interpretation: ctDNA testing identified most cancers that emerged within 18 months in new-onset SSc and DM and stratified near-term cancer risk. These findings support larger, interventional trials to determine whether ctDNA-guided surveillance improves timeliness of cancer detection, optimizes imaging and biopsy strategies, and enhances outcomes in patients with SSc and DM.

after.authors: Russell, M. D.; MacKenna, B.; Goodliffe, S.; Roddy, E.; Abhishek, A.; Rowark, S.; Bechman, K.; Gibson, M.; Brown, J.; Cipolletta, E.; Schaffer, A.; Bacon, S.; Mehrkar, A.; de Lusignan, S.; Coates, L. C.; Cope, A. P.; Norton, S.; Goldacre, B.; Galloway, J. B.
after.abstract: Objectives: To evaluate gout management in England before and after publication of a national clinical guideline by the National Institute for Health and Care Excellence (NICE) and assess the feasibility of using routinely collected health data to monitor guideline implementation at scale. Design: Observational cohort study with interrupted time-series analysis. Setting: Primary care and hospital admission data, with the approval of NHS England. Participants: 22,618,945 individuals aged 18 to 110 years registered with general practices in England contributing data to the NHS OpenSAFELY Data Analytics Service between July 1, 2016, and June 30, 2025. Intervention: Publication of NICE guidance for the diagnosis and management of gout in June 2022. Main outcome measures: Trends in evidence-based measures for gout management, including new prescription of urate-lowering therapy (ULT) and attainment of a target serum urate below 360 micromol/L. Changes in temporal trends after guideline publication were estimated using interrupted time-series models. Results: Of 245,445 individuals newly diagnosed with gout who had available follow-up, 87,885 (35.8%) were prescribed ULT within 12 months of diagnosis. ULT initiation increased from 26.6% in July 2016 to 43.0% in June 2025; however, the rate of increase slowed after publication of the NICE guideline (change in trend: 0.76 percentage-point decrease per year; 95% CI 0.35 to 1.17; p<0.001). Among 108,380 people initiating ULT at any point after diagnosis, 35,865 (33.1%) had at least one recorded serum urate level below target within 12 months of initiation. Urate target attainment improved modestly following publication of the NICE guideline (change in trend: 1.25 percentage-point increase per year; 95% CI 0.64 to 1.86; p<0.001), although sensitivity analyses suggested that was a continuation of an existing trend rather than a guideline-specific effect. Younger adults and males were more likely to be prescribed ULT but less likely to achieve urate targets than older adults and females. Conclusions: Substantial gaps remain between observed gout management and NICE guideline recommendations, particularly for ULT initiation and serum urate target attainment. Guideline publication was not associated with marked improvements beyond existing temporal trends, highlighting the need for implementation strategies to improve gout care. Importantly, routinely collected health data can be used to monitor guideline implementation at scale and identify priorities for improvement.

after.authors: Cassinat, J. J.; Callan, C.; Liggett, C.; Wright, V.
after.author_corresponding_institution: University of Colorado School of Medicine
after.abstract: Objective: To describe how people use the unapproved peptides BPC-157 and TB-500 for tendon, ligament and muscle injury and what side effects they report. Methods: Using a large language model validated against physician review, we analyzed 92,254 posts and comments from 28,652 users in Reddit's peptide communities from 2021 to 2026. We compared side effects with those reported by users of four other peptides in the same communities. Results: In all, 5,588 users described using BPC-157 and/or TB-500 for a specific musculoskeletal injury, most often a chronic tendon problem of the shoulder, knee or elbow. Only 3.8% of users described physician involvement, and 90.9% of those naming a source bought from research-chemical vendors. The median BPC-157 dose (366 mcg per injection) was about 2.7 times the human-equivalent dose of the 10 mcg/kg rat regimen, and among new users it rose from 300 mcg in 2024 to 500 mcg in 2025. Of those stating an outcome, 79.3% reported improvement, and 36.6% of all users were also in physical therapy. Overall, 27.2% described at least one side effect, most often fatigue, anxiety, anhedonia and insomnia. Anhedonia was more common than among users of the four other peptides (10.2% versus 1.3% of those with side effects). Conclusion: Use of these unapproved peptides for musculoskeletal injury is largely unsupervised, relying on grey-market products at self-selected, rising doses without established safety or efficacy.

after.authors: Hong, S. G.; Ryu, D.; Ku, H.; Ko, A.; Oh, J.-I.; Lee, J.; Kang, M.-W.; Kim, M.; Shin, Y.; Lee, H.; Han, S. S.; Kim, Y.; Kwon, J.; Lee, J.; Lee, J.; Park, J. I.; Park, J. T.; An, J. N.; Kim, H. J.; Moon, K.-C.; Kim, Y.-G.; Park, S.; Kim, D. K.; KORNERSTONE investigators,

after.abstract: Background. As kidneys age, their cells change in arrangement and gene expression. Whether these changes are also present in diabetic kidney disease (DKD), and whether they relate to how quickly kidney function is lost, is not known. Methods. Zero-time biopsies from 24 healthy living kidney donors (aged 36-66 years) and biopsies from 28 patients with DKD were profiled by single-cell-level spatial transcriptomics with a 5,101-gene panel. In the donors, we identified how cell neighborhoods and cell-type gene expression change with age and summarized the expression changes as tissue-aging scores. The scores were applied unchanged to DKD and related to the rate of eGFR decline after biopsy in 24 patients, with adjustment for age, sex, baseline eGFR, and proteinuria. We also estimated the scores from routine periodic acid-Schiff (PAS) slides, using models that did not include the patient being scored. Results. In older donors, immune cells were less often found next to tubular epithelium, and contacts between endothelial cells and podocytes and between stromal and epithelial cells were fewer, although cell proportions changed little. Expression of stress-response and cell-cycle regulators (FOXO3, CDKN1A, BBC3, PINK1, IRAK1, SOCS1) increased. Changes in cell contacts in DKD tissue largely followed the same direction as those in older donors. In DKD, higher tissue-aging scores were associated with faster eGFR loss independently of age, sex, baseline eGFR, and proteinuria (overall score, partial {rho} = -0.61); this held for tubular, endothelial, immune, and parietal epithelial cell scores but not for the podocyte score. Scores estimated from PAS slides correlated with the transcriptomic scores (mean {rho} = 0.62) and were also associated with faster eGFR loss (partial {rho}, -0.44 to -0.56). Conclusions. Healthy kidney aging involves a selective loss of cell contacts together with a coordinated stress-response program. DKD kidneys that carry this aging phenotype lose function faster, and the phenotype can be estimated in part from the routine diagnostic PAS slide.

after.authors: Sdoukopoulou, G.; Jahromi, S.; Corona, L.; Partamian, H.; Lim, J.; Afnan, J.; Grova, C.; Papadelis, C.
after.abstract: Neurosurgery is an effective treatment for drug-resistant epilepsy (DRE), but its success depends on the accurate delineation of the epileptogenic focus, approximated noninvasively by electric and magnetic source imaging (ESI/MSI) of high-density electroencephalography (HD-EEG) and magnetoencephalography (MEG). These modalities have distinct sensitivity profiles; consequently, epileptiform activity detected by one modality may remain undetected by the other. However, the implications of these differences for spike detectability and localization accuracy, and the added value of combined electromagnetic source imaging (EMSI), remain insufficiently characterized under clinically realistic conditions. Here, we characterize HD-EEG and MEG sensitivity profiles and compare ESI, MSI, and EMSI, using realistic simulations with known ground truth. We generated HD-EEG and MEG datasets from cortical, insular, and hippocampal sources across multiple orientations, activated using patient-derived intracranial EEG spike waveforms. Spike sensitivity and localization accuracy were evaluated using dipole scanning, dynamic statistical parametric mapping (dSPM), and linearly constrained minimum variance (LCMV). EEG demonstrated higher spike detection rates and sensitivity for radially cortical sources at gyral crowns and sulcal bottoms (p<0.001), while MEG detected more spikes from tangential cortical sources along sulcal walls (p<0.001). MSI localized tangential sources more accurately than ESI across all methods (p<0.001), while dipole scanning outperformed dSPM and LCMV for cortical and insular sources (p<0.001). EMSI outperformed ESI (p<0.001) but did not improve localization over MSI. These findings suggest that complementary anatomical sensitivities of HD-EEG and MEG may improve epileptogenic source characterization, supporting simultaneous acquisition during the presurgical evaluation of patients with DRE.

after.abstract: Amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS) exhibit heterogeneous functional decline, potentially influenced by systemic metabolic reserve. We investigate whether circulating insulin-like growth factor 1 (IGF-1) is associated with subsequent functional change in ALS. Serum IGF-1 was measured in 37 participants with ALS and 25 healthy controls. Baseline levels were compared between groups, and across disease-duration defined progression categories. Lagged regression assessed whether prior visit IGF-1 level predicted change in Revised ALS Functional Rating Scale (ALSFRS-R) on the next visit, adjusting for inter-visit interval, body mass index, age and sex. Mixed-effects and sensitivity analyses assessed robustness. Baseline IGF-1 did not differ significantly between controls and ALS (mean + SD: 107.3 + 54.3 vs 132.2 + 68.3 ng/mL, p = 0.12), or across progression categories (F(2, 34) = 0.13, p = 0.88). Across 48 intervals from 23 ALS participants, each 1-SD higher IGF-1 from prior visit was associated with 1.40-point less subsequent {Delta}ALSFRS-R decline (95% CI: 0.03 to 2.77, p = 0.045). Generalised estimating equations yielded a similar association ({beta} = 1.50, p = 0.030), whereas small-cluster robust inference showed wider uncertainty (p = 0.084). Repeated IGF-1 showed an intraclass correlation coefficient of 0.69, and the lagged association remained positive in all 23 leave-one-participant-out analyses. The IGF-1-by-time interaction was not significant in a random-slope mixed model (p =0.254). Higher circulating IGF-1 may reflect systemic trophic-metabolic reserve associated with short-term functional preservation in ALS, but limited precision precludes definitive prognostic or causal conclusions.

after.title: Preprint: Optimized phase-targeted auditory stimulation reduces nocturnal spikes in childhood epilepsies
after.authors: Schmidt, E. C.; Wapp, N.-A.; Alessandri, B.; Eberhard, R.; Lederberger, D.; Moser, K.; Imbach, L.; Boelsterli-Heinzle, B.; Ramantani, G.; Fattinger, S.; Huber, R.
after.abstract: Interictal epileptiform discharges, so called spikes, are often strongly activated during non-rapid eye movement (NREM) sleep in childhood epilepsies. In children with pronounced spike activation during NREM - sleep, spike burden can be associated with lifelong impaired cognitive functions. This spike activation is also related to alterations in sleep oscillations, specifically slow waves and spindles, which play essential roles in brain maintenance and maturation. These observations suggest that spikes may disrupt sleep-dependent brain processes that are critical for the development of cognitive functions. Phase-targeted auditory stimulation during NREM sleep delivers brief, non-arousing tones at specific phases of ongoing slow waves to modulate sleep oscillations. Recently, our group showed that isolated, less frequent, and thus less expected, tones engage widespread thalamocortical networks, whereas repetitive, regular trains of tones promote habituation and engage more local corticocortical networks. In this study, we use these contrasting stimulation patterns for a targeted modulation of sleep oscillations and examine their interaction with epileptic spikes. In an initial exploratory study (N = 10; age range: 7.3 - 16.2 years), we used a within-night block design to directly compare responses to the different stimulation patterns. Isolated tones delivered at long interstimulus intervals induced a transient increase in spike rate, whereas down-phase stimulation delivered in trains at short, regular intervals was associated with a significant reduction. We subsequently optimized the train-based paradigm and evaluated stimulation delivered throughout the night in a proof-of-concept study using a counterbalanced, between-night design (N = 5; age range: 4.4 - 10.7 years). Spike density decreased locally in all patients, providing convergent evidence for the effects observed in the exploratory study. With this mechanistically guided approach, we demonstrate that repetitive down-phase auditory stimulation of slow waves results in a local reduction of epileptic spikes. This framework may provide a rational basis for targeted interventions aimed at reducing spikes and related cognitive impairments.

after.title: Preprint: Food-Group Intakes and Depression in Tangerang, Indonesia: An Exploratory Case-Control Study
after.authors: Cipta, D. A.; Saputra, A.; Suryadinata, N.; Siregar, R. U. P.; Rivami, D. S.
after.abstract: Background: Diet may be associated with depression, but evidence on locally consumed food groups in Indonesia is limited. Objectives: To compare food-group intake between people with and without a formal diagnosis of depression in Tangerang, Indonesia, and to explore whether BMI modifies any association. Methods: In this case-control study, cases were psychiatric outpatients with a formal diagnosis of depression. Controls had no formal diagnosis and were recruited through university and community networks. Daily intake of ten food groups was estimated with a semi-quantitative food frequency questionnaire. Intakes were compared with independent-samples t-tests (Welch's test when variances were unequal), overall and stratified by BMI group. Logistic regression estimated the odds of depression per 100 g/day of sweetened beverage intake, adjusted for BMI group, sex, and age, with a sweetened beverage and BMI group interaction term. Results: There were 257 participants: 104 cases and 153 controls. Sweetened beverages were the only food group whose intake differed significantly between groups (approximately 214 vs. 153 g/day; mean difference 61 g/day; 95% CI 18-103; p=0.005). Each additional 100 g/day was associated with higher odds of depression after adjustment (OR 1.29; 95% CI 1.09-1.52). The association appeared stronger in underweight/normal-weight participants (ratio of ORs for overweight/obese vs. underweight/normal 0.70; 95% CI 0.49-0.99; p for interaction=0.046). Conclusions: Higher sweetened beverage intake was associated with depression in this sample, and there was modest evidence that the association differed by BMI group. Because the study is cross-sectional in timing, the case-control samples were selected differently, and many comparisons were made, these findings are exploratory. They do not establish causality.

data.summary: added: Preprint: Communication without dialogue? Framing patient-professional interaction in UK institutional discourse on pregnancy loss

after.title: Preprint: Communication without dialogue? Framing patient-professional interaction in UK institutional discourse on pregnancy loss
after.authors: Nuttall, L.; Malory, B.
after.abstract: Communication failures are repeatedly implicated in harmful experiences and outcomes in pregnancy care, especially in contexts of loss, yet little is known about how communication itself is represented in the institutional texts that shape expectations of care. This study examines the extent to which communication is discussed, and how patient-healthcare professional interaction is framed, in publicly accessible UK discourse about pregnancy loss. Two corpora comprising texts from seven medical organisations (120,383 words) and eight charities (224,481 words) were divided into healthcare professional-facing and patient-facing sub-corpora. Frequency, semantic keyness, keyword and concordance analyses were conducted using Wmatrix7. In medical discourse, language and communicative interaction were underrepresented, while speech acts associated with unidirectional professional activities such as advising, recommending and referring were overrepresented. Compared with charity texts, medical outputs foregrounded clinical evidence, policy, risk and professional knowledge. Characteristic forms including 'confirmed', 'advised', 'recommended' and 'offered' frequently occurred in passive or agentless constructions that positioned patients principally as recipients of information; patient agency was most visible in 'reporting' symptoms or concerns. Charity discourse more often foregrounded talking, listening, feelings, preferences, wording, lived experience, and patient knowledge; representing communication as active and bidirectional. We argue that UK medical discourse constructs communication primarily as the transmission of authorised knowledge rather than as relational clinical practice, reinforcing a paternalistic distribution of communicative agency. Medical institutions should embed listening, reciprocal dialogue, sensitivity to language preferences, and checks on understanding as core standards of safe pregnancy care.

after.title: Preprint: Hidden overweight and adverse birth outcomes among Asian mothers in the United States, 2016-2023: a population-based repeated cross-sectional study
after.authors: Tasnim Jahan, J.; Afrose, S.
after.author_corresponding_institution: Department of Epidemiology and Biostatistics, University at Albany, State University of New York, Albany, New York, USA
after.abstract: Background: Standard body mass index (BMI) categories may understate risk in Asian individuals. Lower Asian action points exist, but their relevance to birth outcomes is unclear. Objectives: To estimate the proportion of normal-weight Asian mothers with BMI 23.0-24.9 kg/m2 and its association with birth outcomes, overall and by Asian subgroup, and to compare Asian and White mothers. Methods: Repeated cross-sectional study of US singleton live births, 2016-2023 (National Vital Statistics System). Outcomes were hypertensive disorders, caesarean delivery, preterm birth, and low birthweight. Modified Poisson regression, adjusted for confounders and Asian subgroup, estimated risk ratios (RRs), standardized risks, and risk differences (RDs). We tested for a change in slope at 23.0 kg/m2, subgroup heterogeneity, and race x BMI interaction. Results: Among 1,758,116 non-Hispanic Asian mothers, 314,510 (17.9%) had BMI 23.0-24.9 kg/m2, 30.4% of normal-weight mothers. Compared with BMI 18.5-22.9, standardized risk of hypertensive disorders was 4.5% versus 3.2% (RD 1.4 percentage points, 95% CI 1.3, 1.5; RR 1.44, 95% CI 1.40, 1.47), and of caesarean delivery 32.4% versus 28.6% (RR 1.14, 95% CI 1.13, 1.14). Preterm birth risk was 7.2% versus 6.6% (RR 1.08, 95% CI 1.06, 1.10); low birthweight risk was not higher (7.1% versus 7.5%; RR 0.95, 95% CI 0.93, 0.97). The hypertensive-disorder slope showed no evidence of change at 23.0 (ratio of per-unit RRs 0.99, 95% CI 0.98, 1.01); the hypertensive-disorder RR ranged from 1.24 (95% CI 1.18, 1.29) among Asian Indian to 1.70 (95% CI 1.60, 1.81) among Chinese mothers. BMI-outcome associations differed between Asian and White mothers. Conclusions: Nearly one in three normal-weight Asian mothers had BMI 23.0-24.9 kg/m2, associated with higher risks of hypertensive disorders and caesarean delivery but not low birthweight. The hypertensive-disorder gradient showed no evidence of change at 23.0 kg/m2, and associations varied across Asian subgroups.

after.title: Preprint: Genomic epidemiology reconstructs the pre-detection transmission and establishment of chikungunya virus in Guangdong, China
after.authors: Peng, X.; Chen, Z.; Jia, P.; Zhang, C.; Zhang, M.; Zhong, Y.; Sun, A.; Huang, S.; Li, W.; Zhang, X.; Cai, J.; Liu, Z.; Luo, J.; Su, J.; Sun, C.; Yu, Q.; Tan, Q.; Zheng, Z.; Zou, L.; He, J.; Li, B.; Faria, N. R.; Yu, H.
after.abstract: In 2025, a chikungunya outbreak in southern China resulted in more than 25,000 confirmed cases, but its origins and transmission history remain unresolved. As part of the public health investigation, we generated 1,264 near-complete chikungunya virus (CHIKV) genomes from Guangdong Province and integrated genomic, epidemiological, entomological, and human mobility data to reconstruct the emergence and spread of this outbreak. Our analyses traced the outbreak to a single dominant introduction of a Reunion-associated East/Central/South African (ECSA) virus lineage and dated the origin of the sampled Guangdong outbreak lineage from late April to early May 2025. The interval between the estimated origin of the outbreak lineage and the first reported case was consistent with a period of undetected local transmission and exposed limitations in passive surveillance for early arboviral outbreak detection. Spatiotemporal reconstruction showed two distinct epidemic waves with contrasting transmission dynamics. The Foshan wave involved frequent medium- to long-distance viral movement, while the Jiangmen wave remained relatively localized. Together, these findings reconstruct the early establishment and spatially heterogeneous spread of the largest documented CHIKV epidemic in southern China to date and demonstrate the necessity of expanding active genomic surveillance in areas at the fringe of CHIKV endemic transmission for timely detecting and characterizing emerging epidemics.

after.authors: Zhang, Z.-P.; Larsen, J. T.; Clausen, L.; Agerbo, E.; Bulik, C.; Petersen, L. V.; Yilmaz, Z.
after.abstract: Importance: Severe anorexia nervosa (AN) carries substantial mortality risk, but its consequences associated with social and occupational functioning remain poorly characterized, limiting the development of targeted interventions to improve functioning, prevent and reduce long-term social disadvantage. Objective: To determine whether AN severity is associated with educational attainment, employment, income, and cohabitation status. Design: Cohort study following social and occupational outcomes across adulthood until age 55. Setting: Population-based. Participants: All individuals born in Denmark from 1963 to 1994, alive and residing in Denmark at age 30. The AN group had a first AN diagnosis between ages 10 and 25 years, excluding those who died or emigrated within 5 years. The comparison group had no AN diagnosis. Exposure: Illness severity of AN, measured by the AN Register-based Severity Index 5 years after the first AN diagnosis. Main Outcomes and Measures: Educational attainment was assessed at age 25 (upper secondary education) and at age 30/35 (highest completed education). Employment status, income deficiency, and cohabitation status were assessed annually from age 30 to 55. Results: Among 2,442,916 individuals, 9,465 were diagnosed with AN, of whom 1,996 (21.1%) were classified as severe AN cases. At age 25, individuals with severe AN had increased odds of non-completion of upper-secondary education compared to the general population (odds ratio [OR]=3.07; 95% confidence interval [CI]: 2.72-3.46), and those with less severe AN (OR=1.39; 95% CI: 1.29-1.50). At age 30, severe AN was associated with higher odds of unemployment (OR=3.42; 95% CI: 3.03-3.86), income deficiency (OR=3.84; 95% CI: 3.42-4.31), and living alone (OR=2.43; 95% CI: 2.17-2.71) compared to the less severe AN group. The risk of unemployment and income deficiency diverged across time: individuals with less severe AN gradually approached the general population, whereas those with severe AN diverged further over time. Within the AN cohort, severity differences persisted after adjustment for active AN diagnosis, with minimal attenuation. Conclusions and Relevance: Greater lifetime AN severity was associated with significantly poorer long-term social and occupational functioning outcomes, and these functional difficulties may persist beyond periods of active illness. This vulnerable group needs substantial support in these areas throughout the course of illness.

after.title: Preprint: Classical machine learning versus transformers for predicting daily psychological distress from passive smartphone sensing and self-report: a prospective cohort study
after.authors: Griss Salas, I.; Lam, W.-Y.; Kilshaw, R. E.; Baucom, B. R. W.; de Lacy, N.
after.abstract: Objective: We test whether data collected from daily passive smartphone sensing and self-reports can predict daily significant psychological distress with meaningful potential clinical utility, comparing across best-in-class machine learning algorithms. Methods: In this prospective cohort study, 169 community-dwelling adults completed baseline surveys followed by 7 days of passive smartphone sensing (accelerometer, GPS, power state) and end-of-day Brief Symptom Inventory-18 (BSI-18) assessments. Cases were defined as days (total n = 1,062) where participants' psychological distress measured with the sex-specific BSI-18 Global Severity Index T-score was [≥]63 (prevalence 11.2%). Four classical models (artificial neural network, elastic net, support vector machine [SVM], extreme gradient boosting [XGB]) and four transformers (sensor-only or multimodal; standard or fusion architecture) were tuned, Platt-calibrated and evaluated on held-out participants (210 records, 25 cases) with participant-level bootstrap 95% confidence intervals (CIs). Results: The SVM (area under the receiver operating characteristic curve [AUROC] 0.84; 95% CI 0.71-0.93), the multimodal fusion transformer (0.84; 0.69-0.95) and XGB (0.82; 0.63-0.94) discriminated best; sensor-only transformers performed at chance (0.49-0.50). At the default threshold of 0.50, elastic net logistic regression was the best classifier (sensitivity 0.56, positive predictive value 0.64). At 0.12 (near the outcome prevalence), the SVM detected all cases (negative predictive value 1.00), but positive predictive values were low for all models (0.13-0.26). Decision-curve analysis favored most models over treat-all and treat-none lines at thresholds between 0.05 and 0.25. Baseline survey items, mainly on functional impairment, had the largest feature importance. Conclusions: Compact classical models performed as well as transformers, which were considerably more computationally intensive. Decision-curve analysis supports further clinical exploration of these tools for triaging daily psychological distress, though our results suggest the relative value of psychosocial assessments and digital data should be carefully analyzed. External validation is needed before clinical use.

Decision-curve analysis favored most models over treat-all and treat-none lines at thresholds between 0.05 and 0.25. Baseline survey items, mainly on functional impairment, had the largest feature importance. Conclusions: Compact classical models performed as well as transformers, which were considerably more computationally intensive. Decision-curve analysis supports further clinical exploration of these tools for triaging daily psychological distress, though our results suggest the relative value of psychosocial assessments and digital data should be carefully analyzed. External validation is needed before clinical use.
